thread:
Alex J: FYI got escalation from Acme Ops — after recent IdP change some new hires aren't getting the Editor role via SCIM. They can log in via SSO but permissions are viewer-only. ticket# 98432
Maya C: ok can you paste the SCIM logs from their org? screenshots or the raw PATCH/PUT payload would help.
Acme Ops: here — when we add users to group 'Prod-Engineers' SCIM shows success but role not assigned. sample call: `PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/{id}` body shows members updated, response 200.
Alex J: they also report a deprovision delay: removed from IdP but still active in Redwood for ~30m.
Maya C: that smells like two issues: mapping from group to role not matching (maybe externalGroupName vs externalId) and our async sync worker processing delay. @Jorge R can you check mapping config for that org id=org_77?
Jorge R: looking... their group claim from IdP changed from `Prod-Engineers` -> `prod-engineers` during deploy. Our mapping is case-sensitive when matching `displayName`. I see mapping uses `displayName` -> role 'editor'.
Jorge R: also noticed their provisioning token used in customer SCIM connector was missing `scim:write:groups` scope after they rotated credentials. Their connector still POSTs members but subsequent PATCH to /Users to set role fails with 403. Logs: `403 Forbidden - insufficient_scope: required scim:write:users`.
Priya L: can you dump the exact failing request? a curl would help.
Acme Ops: here's the failing call (redacted):
```
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.example/scim/v2/Users/00uy... \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/scim+json' \
  -d '{ "schemas": [...], "meta":{...}, "roles":[{"value":"editor"}] }'
```
Response: `403 {"error":"insufficient_scope","error_description":"scim:write:users required"}`
Maya C: ok two actionable fixes: 1) re-issue SCIM token with correct scopes (`scim:read users, scim:write users, scim:read groups, scim:write groups`) and update their connector; 2) adjust mapping to match `externalId` instead of `displayName` or normalize casing.
Jorge R: I can do a quick workaround — add a transient mapping entry that matches lowercase displayName for org_77; that'll fix current mismatches while customer rotates token.
Acme Ops: will that also address deprovision lag? user removed from IdP still present in Redwood for ~30m.
Priya L: deprovisioning is handled by the sync worker. It's event-driven but we also have a periodic reconciler every 15 minutes. If their connector successfully calls DELETE or PATCH to remove membership but token lacked write scope it wouldn't reach us. The 30m gap matches the reconciler run window plus retries.
deploy-bot: [event] scim-sync-worker/org_77 processed group update 1812456801 status=200 duration=1.2s
Jorge R: repro steps I used: 1) create SCIM token with only `scim:read` scope, 2) add user to group in IdP, 3) connector sends group PATCH which returns 200 for groups but then token fails on user PATCH -> role missing. Script I used to simulate: `python tools/scim_test.py --org org_77 --token $TOKEN --add-member user_123 --group "Prod-Engineers"`
Maya C: can you attach the scim mapping JSON? we should avoid editing customer mapping directly without consent. Ask Acme to allow a one-time mapping override.
Acme Ops: yes please. if you can temporarily accept lowercase match that fixes rollout for now. we'll rotate token later tonight.
Jorge R: I'll add a temporary mapping rule for org_77 that lowercases displayName and matches `prod-engineers`. Also adding a monitor to alert if a token returns 403 with insufficient_scope more than 3x in 10m.
Priya L: after mapping change, run a manual reconcile for that org: `POST /internal/admin/orgs/org_77/reconcile-scim` (requires platform-admin) — that will force re-eval and apply queued role changes immediately.
Maya C: steps for support to send to customer (short): 1) confirm SCIM token scopes include `scim:write:users` and `scim:write:groups`; 2) verify IdP group claim consistency (case and externalId) or supply externalId mapping; 3) allow temporary lowercase mapping override so we can backfill roles; 4) run manual reconcile after token updated.
Alex J: Acme Ops confirmed they can rotate token now. assigning Jorge to apply transient mapping and Priya to run reconcile once token is in.
Acme Ops: thanks — we'll rotate token at 22:00 UTC and post back here when done. :thumbsup:
Maya C: adding follow up reminders: Jorge -> apply transient mapping (ETA 10m), Priya -> reconcile after token (ETA after 22:05 UTC). I'll close the loop once backfill completes. :eyes:
Jorge R: done — transient lowercase mapping applied at 1812456822, log id=sync-712.
deploy-bot: [alert] scim-token-check/org_77 1812456830 403_count=4 threshold=3 escalated=true
Acme Ops: rotated token, it's updated in their connector.
Priya L: running reconcile now... `POST /internal/admin/orgs/org_77/reconcile-scim` -> 202 accepted, job 9 queued.
deploy-bot: [job] reconcile job 9 completed 1812456844 status=success processed=18 role_changes=16
Maya C: confirmed with Acme — roles backfilled, deprovision gaps resolved. marking ticket# 98432 resolved.
Alex J: nice work, leaving notes in the ticket: root cause = token scope rotation + case-sensitive displayName mapping + reconciler timing. Remediation = token scope check, mapping normalization, and adding token-scope alert.
Maya C: I'll also add a KB doc snippet for support with the curl checks and reconcile command.
Acme Ops: thanks everyone!
